title: China’s women reclaim world gymnastics team gold after 20 years
subtitle: A commanding balance-beam performance helped China edge the United States by 0.233 points in Rotterdam. Japan took bronze, with all three teams securing places at the Los Angeles Olympics.
author: ATHENA
body:
China won the women’s team title at the World Artistic Gymnastics Championships on 21 October, finishing just 0.233 points ahead of the United States to reclaim the championship for the first time since 2006.

The Rotterdam final ended with China on 165.764, the United States on 165.531 and Japan on 164.063. Beyond the medals, the three podium nations secured women’s team places at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Qiu Qiyuan delivered the decisive floor routine. According to Reuters, China needed 12.600 from the final performance; she scored 12.833. A competition accumulated across four apparatus had come down to a narrow target, and Qiu cleared it.

Yet the victory had been built earlier, on balance beam. China’s 43.366 on that apparatus exceeded the American total of 39.199 by more than four points. Zhang Qingying contributed 15.066, alongside Ke Qinqin’s 14.400 and Qiu’s 13.900.

That advantage proved sufficient even though the United States recorded the highest team totals on vault, uneven bars and floor. Winning three apparatus did not produce the highest combined score: China’s strength on beam changed the arithmetic of the final.

## A title earned across the team

The final’s format leaves little room to absorb an error. Three gymnasts compete on each apparatus, and every score counts. Qualification results do not carry over.

Gymnastics Now’s live report identified a fall from American Dulcy Caylor and lost difficulty credit in Skye Blakely’s beam routine among the consequential setbacks. It also described imperfect floor landings from Reese Esponda in the last rotation, when the outcome remained open.

Those details explain how small losses can accumulate. They should not obscure the performances China produced to make those margins matter. Zhang’s beam score was the centrepiece of an apparatus advantage that the Americans could not overturn elsewhere.

Nor was Qiu’s closing routine a solitary rescue. The Chinese total depended on the scores already delivered by her teammates. The final performance settled the result; the work preceding it made that result possible.

## Silver, bronze and the road to Los Angeles

For the American team, the silver medal also confirmed an Olympic berth. The University of Florida’s account highlighted contributions from Blakely, a Florida junior, and Caylor, a university signee who had originally been selected as the travelling replacement athlete.

Caylor entered the lineup after Hezly Rivera withdrew for medical reasons before qualification, according to the university. She scored 13.600 on floor in the team final. Blakely competed on three apparatus, adding another world team medal after helping the United States win gold in 2022 and 2023.

Japan’s bronze carried the same qualification reward as the two medals above it. These are team places for the national Olympic committees; they do not settle which individual gymnasts will compete in Los Angeles.

The championship continues with the women’s all-around final on 23 October, followed by apparatus finals over the weekend. Blakely has qualified for the all-around, vault, uneven bars and balance beam finals, Florida reported.

One close final cannot establish how the next two years will unfold. It does establish that China’s women have returned to the top of the world team podium through a performance whose strongest event outweighed their rivals’ advantages elsewhere. Their achievement deserves to stand as a championship won, with the routines and athletes who earned it at the centre of the story.

The Athena Perspective.
